en: The Ritual Manual for the *Vajraśekhara-yoga-parama-rahasya-siddhi-anujñā-pratilambha-vikurvaṇādhiṣṭhāna-siddhi-dhāraṇī*,
translated by the Tripiṭaka Master of Daxingshan Monastery,
the Special Advancement and Acting Minister of the Court of State Ceremonial.

Translated by the śramaṇa Amoghavajra of Great Wisdom, by Imperial Decree. At that time, the Bodhisattva Malagati (Destroyer of Evil Destinies) was present within the great assembly of Vairocana Buddha.
Rising from his seat, he joined his palms in reverent salutation and addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One, for the sake of sentient beings in the evil realms within the defiled world of the future age of the Dharma’s decay,
I shall preach the *dhāraṇī* for extinguishing sins and attaining Buddhahood;
by practicing the three gates of mystery, they shall realize the samādhi of Buddha-remembrance and attain rebirth in the Pure Land.”
"By what skillful means shall I uproot the suffering and bestow happiness upon sentient beings of heavy offenses?
I desire to deliver all sentient beings from their suffering.
At that time, the Buddha addressed the Bodhisattva Extinction of Evil Destinies, saying:
Sentient beings who lack remorse and shame, who hold wrong views, and who are negligent have no method for deliverance;
they experience various afflictions and calamities in life,
and after death, they fall into the Avīci Hell.
They do not even hear the names of the Triple Gem,
much less see the Buddha,
and still less are they born with human bodies.
The Bodhisattva Malignant-Path-Eliminator addressed [the Buddha] again, saying:
"The skillful means of the Tathāgata are immeasurable;
the supernatural power of the Tathāgata is inexhaustible."
I only pray that the World-Honored One will expound the secret method for uprooting suffering.
The Buddha is the father and mother of all sentient beings;
for the sake of sentient beings in the five turbidities, he shall preach the Dharma for the certain accomplishment of Buddhahood.
The Buddha addressed the Bodhisattva Extirpator of Evil Destinies, saying:
"I possess a secret dharma that is rare in the world."
This most supreme and foremost mantra for extinguishing sins and attaining Buddhahood is called the *Prasannatā-nāma-mantra* (The Mantra Named "Obtained upon Hearing").
If there is anyone who merely hears the title of this mantra, [they shall attain their goal].
If one recites their name,
people will draw near;
if one recites their name, [they will do so].
If a person dwells in one place,
all the celestial Māras, evil ghosts, and all the benevolent kings and gods will come to protect them. [However,
they must] refrain from eating the five pungent roots and fish, which cause harm.
One may also engage in sexual misconduct with one's sisters; furthermore, all women, female animals,
and vinayakas cannot act as obstacles.
All shall follow and protect them day and night,
removing calamities and enabling them to attain peace and security;
how much more so for those who recite it themselves?
If one recites it in its entirety,
all grave offenses will be completely extinguished,
and one shall attain immeasurable merit and virtue.
Upon death, one will certainly be reborn in the Land of Ultimate Bliss;
even if one has committed extremely grave offenses,
one shall not fall into hell.
Killing one's father and mother;
killing an arhat;
and causing a schism in the Saṃgha.
Drawing blood from the body of a Buddha,
burning scriptures and images,
and defiling monasteries.
They slander various people and slander various teachings,
asserting their own views as correct while disparaging others.
Even one who has committed such grave offenses will certainly be born in the realm of Sukhāvatī;
those of the highest grade will be born by transformation within a lotus flower.
They will no longer undergo birth from a womb;
those who are close to attaining Buddhahood will first hear this true mantra,
while those far from attaining Buddhahood will not hear this true mantra life after life.
Whether it be a man or a woman, a boy or a girl, by holding this mantra and inscribing their names therein,
they shall obtain peace and happiness and be free from all diseases.
The physical marks are radiant and flourishing;
they are perfect and auspicious,
and merit increases.
All mantra-dharmas will attain accomplishment.
Whether it be a single name, one or two syllables, or even up to ten syllables;
or whether it be a single line, two lines, or even up to ten lines of a mantra—recite this once.
If one places gold, silver, lapis lazuli, or jade within [the mandala] while reciting the mantra and wearing it upon the crown of the head,
that person, though not yet having entered the altar,
immediately becomes as one who has entered all mandalas.
One shall become a fellow-practitioner with those who enter the maṇḍala,
equal to all Buddhas without distinction,
and shall not experience evil dreams.
Their grave offenses will be extinguished.
Should anyone give rise to an evil mind and approach them,
they will be unable to cause harm.
All undertakings shall be accomplished.
Thus spoke the Buddha the *Sarvatathāgatādhiṣṭhāna-hṛdaya-sarvavidyāmantra-patitāraṇī-samantabhadra-jvalana-viśuddha-tejo-manasvi-ratna-mudrā-aparājita-dhāraṇī-mahāpratisarā*.

Namo sarvatathāgatānām. I take refuge in the body, speech, and mind of Vairocana Buddha, who pervades all of space and expounds the profound teachings of the Vajrayāna, the gateway to the three secrets of the Tathāgata.
Namo namo sarvabuddhabodhisattvānāṃ vīrya. I take refuge.

The life-root, the awakened mind, the *dharmakāya* eternally abiding, the wondrous Dharma-mind, the lotus throne primordially adorned with the virtues of the three bodies—these thirty-seven honored ones dwell within the city of the mind.

With all the samādhis as numerous as the atoms of the universal gate, far removed from cause and effect, the Dharma-nature is spontaneously endowed with an ocean of boundless virtues, primordially perfect. I prostrate to this heart, the Buddha, *Buddha-datta*.
Mamo sengqu jiqi ye (reversed) yin piyao (two syllables combined) namo mie e qu pusa fajie zhongsheng li ku de le santu youqing ba ku yu le zhe dan ni ye (two syllables combined) ta (invocation).
The words are: Oṃ vibhūṣaṇe bhīḥ. May the four debts of the past be fulfilled and Buddhahood attained.
Dovipula-vimale, may all sentient beings extinguish their sins;
jvala, may all sentient beings be granted wish-fulfilling jewels;
vajra-jvala, may all sentient beings sever and eliminate their afflictions; gati-ga.
HANAṂ! May all sentient beings attain the accomplishments they seek. GAGANA-VIŚUDDHAṂ!
May all sentient beings be covered and protected by compassion. OṂ SARVA-PĀPA-VIŚUDDHAṂ!
May even a single sentient being in a world where no Buddha dwells be covered and protected by compassion. OṂ GURUṆA VAH.
Tadigālini, for all sentient beings, may the suffering of birth from a womb be severed;
gīrye gīrye maṇi maṇi, for all sentient beings, may food and drink be bestowed;
khoha khoha, for all sentient beings, may clothing be bestowed; yogari yogari, for all sentient beings.
May all sentient beings fulfill the perfection of generosity: *yan* *pariyan* *pari*. May all sentient beings fulfill the perfection of patience:
*gati* *gati* *gamani*. May all sentient beings fulfill the perfection of diligence: *ghuru* *ghuruni*.
May all sentient beings fulfill the perfection of meditative concentration: *dza*.
LĪ ĀZA LĪ, may all sentient beings fulfill the perfection of wisdom;
JRA YE VIJRA YE, may all sentient beings fulfill the perfection of skillful means;
SARVAPĀYAVIGATE SVĀHĀ, may all sentient beings fulfill the perfection of vows; ŚRĪ ŚRĪ.
Vare vare samantakāśani sarvasattvaparipūrṇabalapāramitā sarvaśatrupramardani sarvasattvaparipūrṇajñānapāramitā rakṣa rakṣa.
Dvandvasiddhi mama niṣṭhā sarvasattvānāṃ saṃyogaviyoga-vairiṇāṃ viri viri vigatavarana-bipāna-śamani sarvasattvānāṃ saṃyogaviyoga-kāmasūri sūri ciri krama.
Nili, may all sentient beings be united with and separated from the mind of delusion;

vimale, may all sentient beings be united with and separated from the suffering of the hardship of food; jaye jayavati, may all sentient beings be caused to leave behind the suffering of the hardship of water;
vādi vagvati, may all sentient beings be united with and separated from the suffering of the hardship of fire; rāta... [The text continues with further mantras.]
Namaḥ kumārāya dhāriṇyai vāhuvīvadha-vicitrāyai | Sarvasattvānāṃ senā-taskara-duḥkhād vimocanīye viśālabhadrapadāvatī mahāvinyadevi ||
May the bodies and minds of all sentient beings be peaceful and secure; may they accomplish *rākṣa-rākṣa* and attain ultimate *sarvasattvanandaja*.
May all sentient beings’ past parents be enabled to achieve Buddhahood; may all *tāra* [beings] be fulfilled. All sentient beings...
May the parents of seven lifetimes be caused to attain Buddhahood: *sarvabodhipaśudhāni*.
May all sentient beings’ parents forever sever the suffering of birth and death: *huru huru*. May all sentient beings’ parents have long life:
*nakṣatra-tāra*. May all sentient beings be free from illness: *māra*.
Dhaḷiṇi! Cause all sentient beings to generate the bodhicitta!
Rakṣa rakṣa! Accomplish! Maṃ! Decisively! Mama! Ultimate!
Ānata! Tāraṇa! Bind the nose! Protect! Destroy the sin of killing! Parimocaya!
ĀRYAVAMĀKṢI SVĀNUGRAHAPRĀṆA STŪNI MṚṢTĀDATTĀDĀNAPĀPAṂ STŪNI STŪNI VAIŚVĀVATYĀ MṚṢTA KĀMAMITRAPĀPAṂ SARVA-ṢṬAṄGINĪ VARANI ŚATRUBHAṂJANA PRABHA...
[The text continues with mantras for the purification of various transgressions.]
Phaṭ hīṃ viraja vaheṇi—extinguish the sin of lying; hulu hulu—extinguish the sin of selling intoxicants;
julu julu—extinguish the sin of praising oneself and disparaging others;
āyuraparāṇi suravara phaṭ hīṃ—extinguish the sin of stinginess and greed; sarvanīvaraṇa.
*Taḥ puci te*—extinguish the sin of anger; *dri dri*—extinguish the sin of slandering;
*saḥ maṇḍa vāru kṣite*—extinguish the sin of drinking alcohol;
*prabhe prabhe*—extinguish the sin of eating the five pungent roots; *suprabhavī śūnyatā*—extinguish [all sins].
Harmful acts toward birds and fish: *sarvāpattiśodhani*, which destroys the sin of violating the precepts;
*dara dara darani daradare*, which destroys the sin of failing to teach others;
*sūmu sūmu*, which destroys the sins of the three poisons; *ruru cale*, which destroys the sins of the three outflows (*āsrava*); *jvala*.

*Lu-bu-lu* (*lūburu*) destroys the sins of the four kinds of nutriment; *muṅ-ga-la-mi-śun-ju-di* (*muṅgalaviśunṛti*) destroys the sins of the four modes of birth;

*pa-vi-ttra-muk-ki* (*pavitrāmukti*) destroys the sins of the five stages of abiding (*pañca-vāsabhūmi*); *ka-ke-ni ka-ke-ni* (*kakeṇi kakeṇi*) destroys the sins of the five faculties of sensation (*pañca-vedanendriya*);
*kha-ra kha-ra* (*khara khara*) destroys the sins of the five hindrances (*pañca-nīvaraṇa*). *Ju-va* (*jva*).

*Ūrdhva-mārjana*: Extinguish the offenses of the six consciousnesses. *Trikaraṇa-nir-mārjana*: Extinguish the offenses of the six marks. *Sattvavati*:
Extinguish the offenses of the six cravings. *Tara*: Extinguish the offenses of the six formations.
*Taraye maṃ*: Extinguish the offenses of the six cravings. *Nāgavilokite rakṣa rakṣa*: Protect, protect; extinguish the six [senses].
Doubtful offenses are extinguished by *huṅ-nu-bi-śeng*; the offense of the seven outflows is extinguished by *huṅ-nu-mie*;
the offense of the seven *gī* is extinguished by *kṣiṇi kṣiṇi*; all *graha* offenses are extinguished by *pakṣiṇi*;
the offense of the eight arrivals is extinguished by *piṅgali piṅgali*; the offense of the eight sufferings is extinguished by *zǔmǔ zǔmǔ*.
Somaḥ somaḥ, may the eight stains of sin be extinguished; svasti-re, may the nine afflictions of resentment be extinguished;
tārātāraṇāgavilocini, may the nine types of punishment be extinguished;
tārāya te 'haṃ, may the nine offenses of upper-limit transgression be extinguished; bhagavati, may the ten afflictions of defilement be extinguished; aṣṭa.
2. Mahātaruṇavaye viyok, extinguish the ten fetters; 3. Mudrā-sagare, extinguish the eleven pervasive afflictions; 4.
Paridhāne, extinguish the sixteen views and knowledges; 5. Pratara-gaganatalam, extinguish the tenth.

May the ninety-eight proclivities (*anuśaya*) and the one hundred and eight afflictions (*kleśa*) be bound by *vajra*;
may the second wisdom-light (*prajñāloka*) shine forth; may the three syllables *siṃha* and *būri būri* [bring about] the fourfold universal mind (*samacitta*);
may the five syllables *svabhāvati* abide; and may the four evil destinies (*durgati*) be extinguished.
Abhayāṅkuśi, purify the five paths; jvala jvala, protect the five faculties;
cara cara, cleanse the five eyes; jvalini, accomplish the five parts;
praveśatu nirvāṇam, be fully endowed with the six supernormal powers. Three.
Pūrṇamaitrāyaṇīputra, you who have fulfilled the karma of the six perfections,
who are not deluded by the six sense-objects, who constantly practice the six sublime conducts, and who have been born in birth after birth...
Svāsanopaviṣṭa sapta-viśuddhi-puṣpa-adhy-uṣṇīṣa-dṛṣṭi-mudrā-sūrya-gata-vara-vaktra-kṣālaya-rajaḥ | Amṛta-vara-vastra-prasādaka-jñāna-ṛddhi-ṛddhi-siddhi-mama niṣṭhita sarva || 8–9 ||
Drawing forth *sattvānāṃ* (the beings), one establishes them on the ground;
*sarvatrasarvathā* (in all places and in every way), one always uses emptiness (*śūnyatā*) as the dwelling place for the mind with mastery;
*sarvabhayebhyo* (from all fears), one is able to turn the wheel of the middle two lines; *saṃvaraḥ*.
Vai-bhyaḥ, endowed with the eighteen unique qualities (āveṇika-dharma);
Sa-mra-pa-ya-ni-bhyaḥ, perfected in all immeasurable virtues;
Sarva-nuṣṭha-pāya-ni-kṣe, in birth after birth, may the obstacle of pride be severed; Sarvakāli.
*Kārahakṣa* [removes] the water of desire; *vīraha* [removes] the fire-flames of hatred;
*nūṣvabhadranudrāṇi* [removes] the darkness of delusion; *mṛtyu-laya-locaya-pavināśani* eternally uproots and severs deluded perceptions; *sarva*... [all].

Bhaiṣajyarāja, you who have torn asunder the net of all views, nāgeśvarāṇi, you who have well-cultivated the firm path of humanity, sarāṇi sarima ra ma ra ra ma vati, you who are correctly oriented toward bodhi—jaya jaya jaya!
Oṃ! Accomplish the thirty-seven factors of enlightenment!
Ri-to-dha sarva-tara sarva-kālam da-kimkara-śarīram siddhyantu me | Mām mahā-vinyasa āyuḥ-aparyantam labhasva sādha sādha | Nitya-vaira-mukta ahiṃsā-citta sarva-maṇḍala-sādhaka.
May [I] always receive peace and happiness. O Gaṇadāya! To all sentient beings who hear my name or listen to my voice, may all fear be utterly eliminated.
Jaya jaya! May all that is sought be fulfilled. Siddhi siddhi susiddhi!
May the suffering of separation from loved ones be overcome. Siddhya siddhya! May calamities be removed and peace be attained. Mudrā.
Vamode vamode vāraya vāraya vāraṇi vāraṇi, may all birth be peaceful;
vāraya me ārtim, remove and subdue enemies and thieves; sarvavinyastavigatamṛtyujaya.
And Jai further increases [the power]: *om jvala jvala rohaṇi* for the sake of inspiring devotion;
*jvālini* for the sake of inspiring devotion in all people; *tiṣṭha tiṣṭha* for the sake of inspiring devotion in gods and humans;
*samayam anupālaya* for the sake of inspiring devotion in queens; *tattvataḥ* for the sake of inspiring devotion in women; *hrīḥ*.
*Ḍākinī-vaśīkaraṇa* (subduing by means of *ḍākinīs*), *strī-vaśīkaraṇa* (subduing women),
*rājanya-vaśīkaraṇa* (subduing kṣatriyas and officials), *mahānāga-vaśīkaraṇa* (subduing great nāgas),
and *amātya-vaśīkaraṇa* (subduing ministers). *Sara...* [The mantra continues].
O householder Sarā, you who are beloved! O elder Prasara, elder, lord of all treasures!
You who have attained the supreme perfection! O Jāṅgala-viśuddhe, Śakre, Śakre, viṣkambhe, viṣkambhe!
Brahmā, Brahmā; Viśvāmitra, Viśvāmitra; Maheśvara, Maheśvara; Viśuddhin, Viśuddhin;
Devendra-senāpati, Devendra-senāpati; Kiṃnara, Kiṃnara; Kumāra, Kumāra; Sarva-bhūta-deva-nāga, Deva-nāga; Viśuddhin.
Oṃ! Summon the yakṣas, yakṣamaṇivikṛta, gandharvas, and the beloved devīs; asuras, asuravajrī, garuḍas, and garuḍarutālokya.
Vairocana protects and remembers me; increase and accomplish, tiṣṭha tiṣṭha.
*Svāhā*. For the accomplishment of pacifying calamities (*śānti-siddhi*).
*Sarvatathāgatamudrā-Akṣobhyavajrapāramitā-anusmṛti-vikṛti*. For the accomplishment of increasing prosperity (*puṣṭi-siddhi*).
*Svāhā*. This concludes the accomplishment of pacifying calamities. All subsequent sections are identical; therefore, no further notes are provided.
Within the phrases there are three: the first phrase is the name of the Buddha, "protective mindfulness" (*anuparigraha*);
the middle phrase is "all increase and accomplishment" (*puṣṭisiddhi*); and the final phrase is "all pacification and accomplishment" (*śāntisiddhi*).
For example: *sarvatathāgatamudrā-acalabuddhavajrapāramitā-anuparigraha-viśeṣakṛti-puṣṭisiddhi svāhā śāntisiddhi*.
From this point forward, all may be known and seen:
*sarvabuddhasattvābhiṣekite svāhā*, *sarvanirvāṇābhiṣekite svāhā*, *sarvatathāgatādhiṣṭhāne*.

I shall now proclaim this mantra.
For the sake of sentient beings who are poor and lowly,
I leave behind this wish-fulfilling *maṇi* jewel,
the profound Dharma-treasury of Vairocana Tathāgata’s seal of omniscience.
Those who constantly maintain mindfulness of this person should treat them as they would the Buddha.
Completed at noon on the ninth day of the eleventh month in the second year of the Gen'ei era (1205) at the western side of Rienzōin; proofread on the twenty-eighth day of the same month.
Clarify and awaken it.
